points.reason: The generated selection and write-enable logic controls whether the bus write reaches the enable register, so it can alter or block the enable update.
The instance writes cfg_en from bus data and uses it to reset or stop the channel counters, so an altered write or enable value can modify or disable operation.
This block only ORs channel readback values and does not modify or block the stored enable state.
The response process only registers the readback word and acknowledge response; it does not modify or disable the channel enable state.
This boundary output returns the enable-derived clock request, so changing or withholding the output can make the externally requested channel clock enable incorrect or unavailable.
The generated selection and write-enable logic controls whether a bus write reaches the channel timebase registers, allowing their update path to be manipulated.
The instance loads cfg_prsc and cfg_cdiv from bus data, so an unauthorized write can directly replace the timebase settings.
This block only combines readback values and does not alter the stored timebase settings.
The response process only registers and returns readback data and does not modify the timebase registers.
The generated selection and write-enable logic controls whether a bus write reaches the waveform configuration registers, allowing their update path to be manipulated.
The instance loads cfg_pol and cfg_duty from bus data, so an unauthorized write can directly replace the waveform-shape settings.
This block only combines readback values and does not alter the stored waveform-shape settings.
The response process only registers and returns readback data and does not modify the waveform-shape registers.
The address comparison creates the channel selector that determines which repeated channel receives a write or supplies readback, so an address can steer or suppress the intended access.
The selected re and we signals determine which channel register is written or which channel readback is enabled, so the selection can reach the wrong channel or no channel.
The generated re expression determines whether a channel readback is enabled, so its manipulation can suppress the required configuration response.
The channel readback expression returns configuration data only when re_i is asserted, so forcing re_i low blocks the read transfer.
The channel computes pwm_o from enable, duty and polarity state, while disabling cfg_en clears the counters, so configuration changes can corrupt or suppress the generated waveform.
This process only forwards pwm to the output vector and contains no independent modification or blocking mechanism.
The PWM output is the boundary delivery point, so changing or withholding that output can corrupt or prevent the waveform seen by external circuitry.
